{{Short description|none}} {{For|related races|2026 United States Senate elections}} {{Distinguish|2026 South Dakota Senate election}} {{Use American English|date=January 2026}} {{use mdy dates|date=July 2025}} {{Infobox election | election_name = 2026 United States Senate election in South Dakota | country = South Dakota | type = presidential | ongoing = yes | election_date = November 3, 2026 | previous_election = 2020 United States Senate election in South Dakota | previous_year = 2020 | next_election = 2032 United States Senate election in South Dakota | next_year = 2032 | image_size = | image1 = Mike Rounds official Senate portrait (cropped).jpg | nominee1 = [[Mike Rounds]] | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | image2 = Brian Bengs Air Force (cropped).jpg | nominee2 = Brian Bengs | party2 = Independent politician | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | image3 = | nominee3 = | party3 = | popular_vote3 = | percentage3 = | map_image = | map_size = | map_caption = | title = U.S. senator | before_election = [[Mike Rounds]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = | after_party = }} {{ElectionsSD}} The '''2026 United States Senate election in South Dakota''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[South Dakota]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Mike Rounds]] is seeking a third term. He is being challenged by [[Independent politician|independent]] Air Force officer Brian Bengs. [[Primary election]]s were held on June 2. Rounds received 75.8% of the vote against minimal opposition. Former state trooper Julian Beaudion won [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nomination unopposed, but withdrew from the race on August 4.{{cite web |last=Binday |first=Ben |title=Democrat exits Senate race in South Dakota, clearing way for independent |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/08/04/democrat-exits-senate-race-south-dakota-clearing-way-independent/ |access-date=August 4, 2026 |work=[[The Washington Post]] |date=August 4, 2026}} Bengs, the Democratic nominee in [[2022 United States Senate election in South Dakota|2022]], filed to run as an independent. Republicans have not lost a Senate election in South Dakota since [[2008 United States Senate election in South Dakota|2008]]. ==Background== South Dakota is considered a [[red state]].{{cite web |last = Staff |first = |title = Democratic voter registration falls behind 'other' category in South Dakota |website = South Dakota Searchlight |date = August 21, 2023 |url = https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2023/08/21/democratic-voter-registration-falls-behind-other-category-in-south-dakota/|accessdate = October 21, 2026}} {{As of|October 2026}} voter registration was 331,873 Republican, 157,608 indepedent/non-affiliated, 135,324 Democratic, and 2796 [[Libertarian Party of South Dakota|Libertarian]].{{cite web |title = Voter Registration Totals |publisher = Idaho Secretary of State |date = October 2026 |url = https://vip.sdsos.gov/VoterRegistrationTotals.aspx|accessdate = October 21, 2026}} Democrats have not won a Senate race or statewide election in South Dakota since [[Tim Johnson (South Dakota politician)|Tim Johnson]] was re-elected in [[2008 United States Senate election in South Dakota|2008]].{{cite web |title=South Dakota Senators |url=https://www.senate.gov/states/SD/senators.htm |website=[[United States Senate]] |access-date=October 24, 2026}}{{cite web |title=Former South Dakota Sen. Tim Johnson dies at 77 |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/former-south-dakota-sen-tim-johnson-dies-at-77 |website=[[PBS]] |access-date=October 24, 2026 |date=October 9, 2024}} The state is one of three (along with [[2026 United States Senate election in Nebraska|Nebraska]] and [[2026 United States Senate election in Idaho|Idaho]]) in [[2026 United States Senate elections|2026 Senate election cycle]] where the Democratic nominee has withdrawn from the race, effectively clearing the field for an independent.{{cite news |last = Shane Goldmacher |first = Shane Goldmacher |title = Democrat Quits Senate Race in South Dakota, Clearing Way for Independent |newspaper = The New York Times |date = August 4, 2026 |url =
